newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa slips back below 890, crosses active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa slips back below 890, crosses active.

text.p: London cocoa futures reversed to end weaker in Friday's cross-dominated dealings after short covering dried up, traders said.
But some traders suggested the day's heavy juggling of positions could be a prelude to a break out of the market's recent gloomy range.
"The market is crossed all over the place," said one trader. "Sometimes people move positions around a bit in anticipation of a big move."

But that was not evident in Friday's performance which left bulls frustrated after second-month May touched 898 for the second time in a row, only to slip back again to a technically disappointing close of 886 stg a tonne, down five.
"There just doesn't seem to be a any impetus to move higher," said one.
Traders said locals had bid the market up initially but New York's losses and lack of follow-up buying turned sentiment down again.

March, which also finished the day down five at 868, was under the spotlight before its first notice day Monday with the nearby structure trading into 14-15 stg from Thursday's 20 with shorts reported to be seeking cover.
Some traders explained the tightening by concerns that one trade house in control of large physical stocks may be long of March and could be seeking delivery.
Others dismissed this, saying a handful of previously complacent shorts were covering positions after a large drop in the open interest earlier this week.
The structure was tighter across the board on Friday.
Turnover reached a strong 13,642 lots. A big cross was cited on the May of 3,475 lots.
CSCE cocoa futures came under further speculative selling with May slipping $14 to $1,289 at 1745 GMT.
Technically, May's finish below 890 will be seen as discouraging, but the market may renew attempts to overcome 900 on the close next week.
